                                 ORDER

(Per: Ms. Kumkum Rani, President):

Both these appeals under Section 41 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 have been directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 28.06.2021 passed by learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Haridwar (hereinafter to be referred as "The District Commission") in consumer complaint No. 408 of 2019, styled as Sh. Vinay Jain Vs. Sant Sales and another, wherein and whereby the consumer complaint was allowed. For the sake of convenience, First Appeal No. 138 of 2021; Whirlpool of India Vs. Sh. Vinay Jain and another, is taken as a leading appeal, for the disposal of the instant appeals. Since both the above-mentioned appeals have arisen out of the same judgment and order, hence both are decided together by this common judgment.

2. The facts giving rise to the present appeals, in brief, are, as such that on 07.10.2012, the complainant - Sh. Vinay Jain had purchased a washing machine from opposite party No. 1 - Sant Sales, the authorised 2 First Appeal No. Whirlpool of India 22.05.2024 138 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another And First Appeal No. Sant Sales 22.05.2024 184 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another dealer of opposite party No. 2 - Whirlpool of India Limited, upon cash payment of Rs. 23,500/-. The subject washing machine carried two years' warranty. The complainant had also entered into contract of AMC (Annual Maintenance Contract) for the year 2014 to 2019. It was alleged that the complainant felt an issue in the washing machine on 08.04.2019 and the opposite parties gave false assurance of repairing the washing machine. The complainant lodged another complaint for service request on 19.09.2019 vide complaint No. DN0919001774, which was replied through e-mail dated 17.10.2019, falsely stating that the defective part of the washing machine is not available and offered only 25% price of the washing machine subject to payment of transportation charges of Rs. 1,000/-, while the warranty of the washing machine was still in force. The said offer was not at all acceptable to the complainant because he was entitled to get the washing machine duly repaired from the opposite parties or replacement thereof with a new one. On account of act of the opposite parties, the complainant had suffered mental, physical and financial agony. There has been deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties. Therefore, the consumer complaint was submitted before the District Commission.

3. The opposite party No. 1 - Sant Sales did not appear before the District Commission and did not submit any written statement. Therefore, the District Commission vide order dated 07.07.2020 closed the opportunity of filing the written statement by the opposite party No. 1.

4. The opposite party No. 2 - Whirlpool of India Limited submitted written statement before the District Commission and conceded manufacturing of the subject washing machine as well as purchase of washing machine by the complainant on 07.10.2012. It was pleaded that a complaint regarding defect in the washing machine was lodged 3 First Appeal No. Whirlpool of India 22.05.2024 138 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another And First Appeal No. Sant Sales 22.05.2024 184 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another in the year 2019, after expiry of warranty period of two years'. There has not been any deficiency in service on the part of the manufacturing company and the complainant is not entitled to get any relief. The consumer complaint is liable to be dismissed.

5. The District Commission, after hearing learned counsel for the complainant & opposite party No. 2 and after perusing the material available on record, allowed the consumer complaint vide impugned judgment and order dated 28.06.2021, thereby directing the opposite parties (appellant in both the appeals before us) to refund the price of the washing machine amounting to Rs. 23,500/- to the complainant, who has been arrayed as respondent No. 1 in the present appeals, together with interest @6% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint, i.e., 26.12.2019 till final payment and also to pay an amount of Rs. 50,000/- towards mental, physical and financial agony; Rs. 15,000/- towards litigation charges & counsel fee, besides to pay Rs. 5,00,000/- towards special damages.

6. On having been aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order, the present appeals have been set in motion. First Appeal No. 138 of 2021 has been filed by Whirlpool of India and whereas First Appeal No. 184 of 2021 has been preferred by Sant Sales.

7. In the memo of First Appeal No. 138 of 2021, it has been stated by the appellant - Whirlpool of India (manufacturing company) that the impugned judgment and order passed by the District Commission is grossly erroneous & untenable in law and is also against the facts, documents, evidence and circumstances of the case and has been passed without application of mind. It was further contended that the washing machine after having been purchased by the complainant in the year 2012, was reported to be defective in the year 2019, after expiry period 4 First Appeal No. Whirlpool of India 22.05.2024 138 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another And First Appeal No. Sant Sales 22.05.2024 184 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another of manufacturing warranty of two years', which under no stretch of imagination, tantamount to goods to be defective or the complainant falls under the ambit of "consumer". It was further submitted on behalf of the appellant that the District Commission has wrongly held that the complainant falls within the ambit of "consumer", after a lapse of 7 years' of the product having been purchased or on account of non-availability / non-replacement of the parts after 7 years' of smooth running of the washing machine, tantamount to deficiency in service. Learned counsel for the appellant has also stated that learned District Commission has failed to appreciate that the warranty period of washing machine ended within two years' from the date of purchase and what continued was the Annual Maintenance Contract, which was nothing, but an optional maintenance contract, wherein on the basis of service plan chosen, the coverage was provided. The complainant chose the plan for a period of 12 months' from 27.09.2018 to 26.09.2019 and the complainant had used the washing machine not only during the whole warranty period without any issue, but all through the AMC as well, as in para 1 of the consumer complaint, the complainant has mentioned that he felt the issue in the washing machine on 08.04.2019, i.e., after the expiry of approximately 7 years' from the date of purchase of the washing machine. Learned District Commission has gravely erred in coming to immediate conclusion that the machine is being continuously malfunctioned, overlooking the averments made in the consumer complaint. The District Commission has passed the impugned judgment and order without considering the actual facts. The impugned judgment and order is against law, facts and merits of the case, hence the same is liable to be set aside.

8. In the memo of First Appeal No. 184 of 2021, the appellant - Sant Sales has stated that the impugned judgment and order is not in accordance with law and learned District Commission has passed the 5 First Appeal No. Whirlpool of India 22.05.2024 138 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another And First Appeal No. Sant Sales 22.05.2024 184 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another impugned judgment and order beyond the facts and merits. It has further been stated that learned District Commission has failed to consider that no notice of the consumer complaint was served upon the appellant, nor the same is reflected from the order-sheet of the consumer complaint, nor there is a finding of service being sufficient upon the appellant. The District Commission has committed perversity in entertaining the consumer complaint, which was hopelessly time barred. The District Commission has committed perversity in passing the impugned judgment and order, believing the contentions of the complainant. The District Commission has failed to exercise the jurisdiction vested in it by law and has exercised the jurisdiction not vested in it by law. Hence, the impugned judgment and order has been passed with an erroneous observation, which can not be sustained in the eyes of law. Therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.

9. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record. It is admitted that the complainant had purchased the subject washing machine from opposite party No. 2 on 07.10.2012 for sum of Rs. 23,500/-, carrying two years' warranty. It is also admitted that the complainant had taken AMC (Annual Maintenance Contract) for the year 2014 to 2019. Now the question arises as to whether the AMC taken by the complainant amounts to extension of period of warranty of the subject washing machine or not. As stated above, it is an admitted fact that the warranty of the subject machine was for a period of two years' from 07.10.2012, i.e., the date of purchase and after the expiry of period of warranty, the AMC opted for / taken by the complainant, can not be reckoned as extension of warranty, as has wrongly been held by the District Commission.

10. The next contention raised on behalf of the manufacturing company was that under the AMC, only few parts are covered which are specifically mentioned under the contract of AMC. The parts covered for free replacement under AMC are as follows:

(a) Semi-Automatic - Wash motor, spin motor, wash timer, spin timer, drive assembly and capacitor.
(b) Fully Automatic - Motor, Pressure Sensor, TSP (Drive assembly), capacitor, Inlet valve, suspension rod (assembly), PCB.

11. It is further contended that after continuous use of the product for 7 years', the complainant is not entitled to replacement of the product or refund of the price thereof. It is correct to say that after 7 years' of use of the product, without submitting any expert report on behalf of the complainant regarding inherent manufacturing defect in the machine, the refund of the cost of the product can not be ordered, particularly in view of the fact that the warranty period of the machine had already expired and the AMC taken can not be termed as extension of warranty period. It is established on record that the washing machine did not become non-functional during the warranty period of two years' given at the time of purchase of the product. The complainant has himself admitted in the consumer complaint that the warranty of the washing machine was for a period of two years'. In the case of Stereocraft Vs. Monotype India Ltd., Vohra House, New Delhi reported in (2000) NCJ (SC) 59, the defect in the goods occurred after several years of running. It was held by Hon'ble Apex Court that the terms of guarantee do not cover replacement after expiry of 12 months' and the complainant can not claim the goods to be defective or a consumer under the Act. The complainant has nowhere mentioned in 7 First Appeal No. Whirlpool of India 22.05.2024 138 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another And First Appeal No. Sant Sales 22.05.2024 184 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another the consumer complaint that the subject product suffers from inherent manufacturing defect. Thus, in the given circumstances, without cogent proof of manufacturing defect in the washing machine in question, the replacement thereof with a new one or refund of its price can not be ordered. Therefore, the appeal filed by the manufacturing company deserves to be allowed.

12. So far as First Appeal No. 184 of 2021 filed by Sant Sales is concerned, a perusal of the order-sheet of the consumer complaint annexed with the memo of appeal, has revealed that the service of notice of the consumer complaint upon the appellant was not considered to be sufficient and vide order dated 07.07.2020, the opportunity of filing the written statement was closed and vide subsequent order dated 25.01.2021, the opportunity of filing the evidence was closed by the District Commission. We have, however, dealt with the matter on merits and since the manufacturing defect in the subject washing machine has not been proved by the complainant, it would not be in the interest of justice to remand the case back to the District Commission to decide the consumer complaint afresh, on account of the impugned judgment and order being ex-parte against the dealer - Sant Sales. Thus, the appeal filed by the dealer also deserves to be allowed.

13. For the reasons aforesaid, we are of the view that the impugned judgment and order has been passed by the District Commission without application of mind. We are also of the considered opinion that the complainant has failed to prove any deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties to the consumer complaint, who are appellants before us. Hence, the impugned judgment and order passed by the District Commission is totally unjustified and the District Commission has exercised the jurisdiction not vested in it by law and has acted with 8 First Appeal No. Whirlpool of India 22.05.2024 138 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another And First Appeal No. Sant Sales 22.05.2024 184 of 2021 Versus Sh. Vinay Jain and another material illegality and infirmity, while passing the impugned judgment and order. Thus, we are inclined to interfere with the finding recorded by the District Commission. Therefore, the appeals is liable to be allowed.

14. Appeals are allowed. Impugned judgment and order dated 28.06.2021 passed by the District Commission is set aside and consumer complaint No. 408 of 2019 is hereby dismissed. No order as to costs of the appeals. The amount deposited by the appellants with this Commission in their respective appeals, be released in their favour.

15. A copy of this Order be provided to all the parties free of cost as mandated by the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 / 2019. The Order be uploaded forthwith on the website of the Commission for the perusal of the parties. A copy of this Order be sent to the concerned District Commission for record and necessary information.

16. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this Order.

17. A copy of this judgment be kept on the record of connected First Appeal No. 184 of 2021.
